regions.name: 구겨진 종이굴
regions.prompt:
Transform the supplied approved concept into a PRODUCTION GROUND MATERIAL STRIP for a 2D tilemap. Output a single 3:1 wide image. The ENTIRE rectangle is solid material cross-section, all the way from its very TOP border to its bottom. NO empty cave air, NO background, NO scene, NO ceiling, NO platform silhouette in the middle, NO panel layout, NO grid, NO labels or text. The image TOP BORDER itself is the walkable contact line. At the extreme top show a very thin softly uneven worn material edge. Below it long low-contrast strata flow across the FULL width, interrupted asymmetrically by calm planes and a few soft material folds. No individual central boulders, no evenly spaced motifs, no cell-sized repetitions. This artwork will be mechanically divided into twelve adjacent 128px cells, with each group of four cells sharing a broad flowing feature; NEVER draw cell boundaries.
Preserve the supplied image's graphite-gray 2D game illustration style, 70 percent detail, broad matte shapes and softly worn edges. Reduce microtexture, grain, scratches and tiny cracks. Lighting neutral and subdued, no spotlight. At top material is readable light-mid gray, fade GRADUALLY and CONTINUOUSLY downward into almost-black throughout the entire image height, bottom 15 percent near-black. Full width shares the same depth falloff. Left and right ends should blend naturally for horizontal repeat, without borders. The strip is solid terrain, no transparencies, no gaps, no white background. Do NOT recreate the reference scene; extract and redesign only its continuous floor material.
Material: compressed graphite soil with broad worn paper strata. Soft folded overlapping paper lips irregularly cross the strip, mostly quiet low-contrast masses. Sparse blunt rootlets, no long stringy detail. Lightest and softest of these nearly monochrome subareas.

conceptPrompts.name: 흑연 광산
conceptPrompts.prompt:
Use the supplied image ONLY as the approved material-rendering and art-direction reference for our original game Unfinished Sketchbook. Generate a NEW matching subarea concept, not a copy of its rock pattern. Single wide 16:9 side-scrolling 2D game terrain study, no collage. Same polished subdued stylized illustration, about 70/100 detail and 75/100 realism: broad matte planes, soft worn rounded forms, no photographic grit or dense thin scratches, no pixel art, no sketch hatching. The entire first region remains nearly monochrome graphite gray; only tiny temperature differences, no saturated colors.
Show readable foreground floor and a connected low raised ledge or wall bend, with quiet enclosed-cavern backdrop. The ground fills lower 45 percent of the frame; strict orthographic side elevation, no perspective top faces. Surface relief shallow, walking contour thin and irregular, no smooth thick trim. Soft rounded inner and outer corners. Texture must flow across 12-15 imagined 128px cells without cell boundaries, repeating central motifs, rows of rocks, periodic ovals, or evenly spaced decoration. Use sparse clusters of different scales, long material flows and large calm regions. Continuous material shading from readable surface into almost black deep ground, no per-cell gradients. Backdrop is lower contrast than playable terrain. No sky, landscape horizon, character, text, UI, numbers, grid, diagram or watermark. These are terrain-direction samples, not an exact existing room layout and not a tile atlas.
SUBAREA: Graphite Mine. Distinct from soft paper cavern: dense compressed graphite sediment, broad rounded dark slate layers, a few long discontinuous mineral bands and worn broad extraction scars. Layers are low-angle irregular strata passing through many imaginary cells, not sharp crystal spikes, polygon shards, cobblestones or scattered rubble. Dark neutral-cool gray, occasional satin graphite gray planes but no metallic glare. Mostly level sturdy mine floor bends into a short raised bank on the right. One shallow dark-ink depression off-center is embedded in the land, small and unobtrusive, with a dull subdued glint. Quiet low-ceiling tunnel silhouette in back, only one or two faint irregular old supports as background cues; ground is the main subject. No glowing ore, crystals, lamps, rails or industrial machinery. Retain subtle hints of compressed paper so it belongs in the same world as the reference, but graphite mass dominates. The result should read as a slightly denser, colder and more compressed sibling of the approved image.

SUBAREA: Inside the Sketch Tree. Same graphite-paper world, but the land becomes old graphite-stained wood with broad softened grain: long sweeping wood fibers curve horizontally along the floor then vertically up a thick connected side wall, with only one subdued off-center knot and a few smooth layered bark lips. Forms interlock and cross many imaginary cells. Keep shapes solid and substantial, not a pile of logs, a wooden plank floor, repeated knots, thin scratchy grain or dense roots. Near-monochrome ash-gray with a very faint warm-gray wood undertone, never orange or brown fantasy forest. Foreground floor lower half, one rounded upward-growing ledge on the left joins a thick trunk wall; open play air center/right. Background has faint vertical hollow-trunk ribbons hinting at the tall climb, but no visible sky or outdoor foliage. Just one short broad branch-derived shelf can emerge from the side wall above the main floor, with worn rounded tip. Preserve generous calm negative space, the approved reference's material restraint and black depth fade. This must read as wood/graphite growth rather than ordinary rock.

SUBAREA: Tangled Root Depths, the late-region boss approach. Graphite earth bound by a few thick ancient root masses. Broad flattened and softened roots merge into the floor and curve around a rounded low wall on the right; several roots pass over and under each other at uneven intervals across many cells. Root strands vary widely in width and dissolve into calm black soil. No repeated braided rope border, no row of knots, no hairlike spaghetti, no thorns, no needle spikes. Slightly darker than the reference, neutral charcoal with faint cool-gray graphite edges; no red, purple or blue magical glow. The walking edge remains mostly level with shallow irregular soil lumps, never a line of cylindrical roots serving as a bumpy fence. Root silhouette in far background vaguely suggests a closed-in nest/arched chamber, subtle enough not to compete with the foreground. One or two small matte ink-stained seams appear deep in the cross-section. Threat comes from mass, compression and darkness, not fine detail. Keep the near-surface mass readable while its full depth gradually sinks into nearly invisible black. This is a restrained material variation in the same region, not an entirely different monster biome.
